newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-OSGOOD BLANKS FLAMES AS YZERMAN PLAYS 1,000TH GAME.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-OSGOOD BLANKS FLAMES AS YZERMAN PLAYS 1,000TH GAME.

text.p: Chris Osgood turned aside 28 shots to record his fifth shutout of the season and Tomas Sandstrom scored twice as the Detroit Red Wings blanked the Calgary Flames 4-0 on Wednesday.
Detroit captain Steve Yzerman picked up three assists in the 1,000th regular-season game of his career and Vyacheslav Kozlov set up two goals for the Red Wings.
"I think to the players it means a lot for a guy to get 1,000, but it's really no big deal," Yzerman said.
"You kind of reflect on all the guys you've played with. Doing it with one team is something I'm proud of."
Sandstrom, who has four goals and three assists over the last six games, gave Osgood all the offence he would need when he beat Calgary goaltender Trevor Kidd with 8:23 left in the first period.
His second goal at 5:10 of the second made it 3-0.
Darren McCarty and Nicklas Lidstrom scored the other Detroit goals.
Kidd faced 38 shots and finished with 34 saves as the Flames saw their season-high six-game unbeaten streak halted.
In Edmonton, Mariusz Czerkawski recorded his first career hat trick as the Oilers built a five-goal lead before hanging on for a 6-5 victory over the Toronto Maple Leafs.

Czerkawski tallied twice in a three-goal first period and completed his hat trick 2:13 into the second. He also assisted on Dean McAmmond's goal just over seven minutes later that gave Edmonton a commanding 6-1 lead.

The Maple Leafs put together a furious rally with the help of three powerplay goals, including Wendel Clark's second tally of the game at 12:56 of the third that pulled Toronto within one. Doug Gilmour contributed four assists for Toronto.
Edmonton goalie Curtis Joseph was victimised for four unanswered goals but made a pad stop on Mats Sundin's point-blank shot with 1:15 left to preserve the win.
At New Jersey, Adam Graves scored midway through the second period to lift the New York Rangers into a 1-1 tie with the New Jersey Devils, who extended their team-record unbeaten streak to 12 games.
Graves took a pass from Brian Leetch and swept the puck with his backhand past goaltender Martin Brodeur's stick with 11:30 to go in the second period to knot the score.
Steve Thomas beat Rangers goalie Mike Richter at 12:44 of the first period with the lone goal for New Jersey, which is 6-0-6 in its last 12 games.
Brodeur finished with 22 saves, while Richter stopped 31 shots, including two key saves in overtime.
In Philadelphia, Kevin Dineen scored twice, including the tying tally late in the second period, as the Hartford Whalers skated to a 2-2 deadlock with the Flyers.
Former Flyer Dineen took a pass from Andrew Cassels and wristed a shot through goaltender Garth Snow's pads with 2:24 left in the second period for his second goal of the game and 15th of the season.
John LeClair and Petr Svoboda scored for the Flyers, who welcomed Eric Lindros back to the lineup.
Jason Muzzatti made 23 saves for the Whalers, while Snow stopped 24 shots.
